title: The Lion of Mewar
summary: Maharana Pratap was a Hindu Rajput king of Mewar, a region in modern-day Rajasthan, India. He is known for his military resistance against the Mughal Empire, particularly his role in the Battle of Haldighati.

events.title: Birth of Pratap Singh
events.description: Pratap Singh was born in Kumbhalgarh Fort to Udai Singh II and Jaiwanta Bai.  Kumbhalgarh served as an important refuge and military stronghold for the Mewar kingdom.

events.title: Accession to the throne
events.description: Following the death of Udai Singh II, Pratap Singh ascended to the throne of Mewar at Gogunda.  He inherited a kingdom facing constant pressure from the expanding Mughal empire.

events.title: Initial diplomatic missions from Akbar
events.description: Emperor Akbar sent a series of diplomatic envoys, including Raja Man Singh, to persuade Pratap to accept Mughal suzerainty.  Pratap refused to bow to Mughal rule, marking a clear path toward inevitable conflict.

events.title: Battle of Haldighati
events.description: Maharana Pratap led his forces against the Mughal army led by Raja Man Singh at Haldighati. Although outnumbered, the Rajputs fought fiercely, but the battle ultimately resulted in a Mughal victory.

events.title: Recapture of Kumbhalgarh
events.description: After a period of Mughal occupation, Pratap managed to recapture the strategic Kumbhalgarh fort. This victory boosted the morale of his forces and demonstrated his resilience.

events.title: Shift to Guerrilla Warfare
events.description: Recognizing the limitations of conventional warfare against the Mughals, Pratap adopted guerrilla tactics. His forces harassed Mughal supply lines and outposts, weakening their control over the region.

events.title: The Bhama Shah Assistance
events.description: Bhama Shah, a wealthy merchant and minister, provided Pratap with substantial financial assistance. This allowed Pratap to rebuild his army and continue his resistance efforts. This significantly boosted his morale and resources.

events.title: Recapture of Chittorgarh
events.description: Pratap successfully recaptured significant portions of Mewar, including Chittorgarh (though without reclaiming Chittorgarh Fort itself). This marked a turning point in the conflict, showcasing Rajput resilience.

events.title: Establishment of Chavand
events.description: Pratap established Chavand as his new capital.  He dedicated time to developing art and culture in the region, contributing to its prosperity until his death.

events.title: Death of Maharana Pratap
events.description: Maharana Pratap died at Chavand, leaving behind a legacy of courage and resistance against Mughal rule. He is revered as a symbol of Rajput valor and independence.
